description: Machine-readable semantic capability profiles for the 17 executable minimal-generator implementations. Every field marked provenance='oracle' was determined by measurement against an independent oracle (tools/validate_*.py), not read off the algorithm's title or its source paper.

family_relation._comment: satisfies[emitted][requested] -> how an implementation emitting `emitted` can serve a request for `requested`. exact = identical family; post_filter = requested family is recoverable by a documented filter on the output; no = different question.

post_filters.ghui->high_utility_generator: retain X with u(X) >= theta; verified exactly equal to HUG-Miner output (687 at theta=100, 1475 at theta=50 on foodmart)
post_filters.generator_closure_pairs->minimal_generat: project each class onto its generator list
post_filters.generator_closure_pairs->closed_itemset: project each class onto its closure
post_filters.minimal_generator->disjunction_free: disjunction-free sets are a proper subset of the generators; requires an inclusion-exclusion test per candidate

conventions.boundary_evidence: oracle: on Connect at minsup=0.4 (27022.8) DefMe returns 3 itemsets of support exactly 27023 that the ceil-boundary miners omit

validation.scope: 58 transactional configurations; set-level equality on mushroom/0.4 and chess/0.7

notes: Highest robustness among JVM transactional miners: completed all 58 configurations.

conventions.boundary_evidence: oracle: on Chess at minsup=0.7 (2237.2) returns 99 itemsets of support exactly 2237 that the native post-filters omit

completeness.hazard: At k >= 2 the released binary applies an inclusion-exclusion test (calc_subset_sum, PatternSet.cpp:346,440) that characterises the strictly smaller DISJUNCTION-FREE family. Output stays sound but returns ~40% of the generators, and runs faster for exactly that reason. The parameter is undocumented.
completeness.evidence: oracle: mushroom/0.2 returns 683 of 1703 generators at k=100

validation.oracle: vertical bitset support oracle + set equality against DefMe

notes: Fastest dedicated generator miner and lowest peak memory, but native C++ so the advantage is not attributable to algorithm design alone.

conventions.empty_set_rule: emitted iff the dataset contains NO full-support item. Mushroom has item 90 in all 8416 transactions, so the empty set is omitted there but emitted on the other six datasets.

soundness.evidence: oracle: on mushroom/0.05, 2960 of 24350 returned itemsets have a proper subset of equal support

notes: The defect is shared with TalkyG_Diffset and is therefore located in the common generator test, not in the TID-list representation.

soundness.evidence: oracle: output identical to Talky-G on every configuration

validation.scope: set equality against DefMe on mushroom/0.4 and chess/0.7

notes: Writes all frequent itemsets tagged '#IS_GENERATOR: true|false'; a plain line count counts frequent itemsets, not generators.
Breadth-first: times out on dense data.

notes: Emits a human-readable closed-set + generator report; a plain line count includes headings.
Lowest completion rate of the transactional family (69.0%).

validation.scope: ~27000 itemsets across mushroom/0.4 and chess/0.7, 0 violations

notes: Post-filtering baseline: mines all frequent itemsets, then discards non-generators. Not a dedicated generator algorithm and not part of the 25-algorithm taxonomy.
Post-filtering baseline.
Post-filtering baseline; fastest single implementation overall on the transactional grid.

conventions.boundary_evidence: oracle: on sign/0.03 (threshold 21.9) FEAT retains patterns of support 21

notes: Output byte-identical to FSGP on all 16 configurations, but 3.4x slower.
Lowest peak memory of the sequential family (520 MB mean).
Fastest sequential generator miner (2.98 s mean); identical output to FEAT.

conventions.boundary_evidence: oracle: on sign/0.03 (threshold 21.9) VGEN's effective floor is 22; all 3802 patterns it omits relative to FEAT/FSGP have support exactly 21. Same at 0.04 (128 omitted, all at support 29, threshold 29.2).

completeness.hazard: Returns strictly fewer patterns than FEAT/FSGP whenever sigma*|D| is non-integral. This is a boundary convention, not an incompleteness bug: every pattern it returns is a genuine generator, and every pattern it omits sits exactly on the rounded threshold.

notes: Highest peak memory of the sequential family (1147 MB mean, 3046 MB peak).
Best runtime-memory trade-off among the evaluated high-utility methods.
Prints '#SUP:' as the database size rather than the pattern's support - a display quirk, not a data defect.
Emits support-minimal itemsets whose CLOSURE is high-utility. Strict superset of HUG-Miner: filtering to u(X) >= theta reproduces HUG's output exactly (687 at theta=100, 1475 at theta=50).

soundness.summary: Despite its name, this implementation returns NO support-minimal generators. Its minimality is defined with respect to utility.
soundness.evidence: oracle on foodmart/theta=50: of 2002 returned patterns, 0 are support-minimal and 0 are closed, but 1976 (98.7%) are minimal with respect to utility (no immediate subset reaches the threshold).
soundness.consequence: Its pattern counts are NOT commensurable with HUG-Miner's or GHUI-Miner's and must not be tabulated in the same column.

notes: The paper grouped this with HUG/GHUI before the audit; the grouping was corrected.

validation.oracle: vertical bitset support oracle + closure verification
validation.scope: mushroom/0.4 (124 classes, 153 generators) and mushroom/0.3 (425 classes, 544 generators); 1246 checks, 0 discrepancies

notes: The only implementation emitting generator-closure PAIRS, so both halves are independently checkable.
The harness runs it with window size = |D|, so its output is directly comparable with static generator miners.
Streaming/sliding-window operation is its actual design target and is NOT exercised by this benchmark.
Must be launched with an absolute path; a relative forward-slash path fails CreateProcess on Windows.

implementations.provenance: SPMF v2.65 (AprioriRare; the MRG-Exp variant is not separately exposed)

conventions.boundary_evidence: oracle: rarity is supp(X) < sigma_max*|D|, but no returned itemset ever sits between floor and ceil of that value, so the output does not discriminate the two roundings. Every verdict below was re-derived under BOTH and holds under both.

completeness.note: Arima is the only implementation for which COMPLETENESS is checkable rather than merely soundness: minimal rare itemsets are exactly the negative border of the frequent family, so every one has the form F + {i} for a frequent F, and the true family can be enumerated in full and compared as a set.

validation.scope: the 11 configurations Arima completes; set-equal to the oracle enumeration wherever the candidate space is tractable, sound everywhere

operational_hazard.summary: Aborts on dense data through candidate explosion, not through a JVM heap ceiling.
operational_hazard.evidence: 5 of 21 runs abort at the default heap; re-run at -Xmx12g only 1 of the 5 recovers (chess maxsup=0.3: 107 s, 8.2 GB, 180161 generators), the other 4 abort again at 11.1-11.8 GB after 14-23 min.

notes: Parameter is a MAXIMUM support threshold, not a minimum.
Usable on sparse data only.
